description:
Under Option B, no bulk private history is published — only the working
tree (via the final curated sync in Phase 4) and the _project/** subtree
history (via filter-merge in Phase 4). Audit scope shrinks accordingly:
the only paths whose contents land on public are the ones in scope here.

Risks audited:
1. Secrets in the working tree of any path that will land via the final
   curated sync (i.e., everything except .claude, .codex, .gemini, secrets)
2. Secrets in the commit history of _project/** (which WILL be published
   via filter-merge if D2a stays on its recommended choice)
3. Internal commentary, stakeholder names, vendor complaints in _project/,
   _blog/drafts/, code comments
4. Embarrassing or rough commit messages on _project/** specifically
5. Divergence between private working tree and public mirror history
   (any commits made only on the public mirror that should be replicated
   on private before the final sync)

Outcome: either go-ahead, or a remediation plan (fix files in working
tree, scrub _project/** history with filter-repo, drop _project/** to
working-tree-only sync, etc.) before proceeding to Phase 1.

Plan file: /Users/joe/.claude/plans/single-repo-migration.md (Phase 0).

anti_patterns.dont: audit commit messages on the full repo
anti_patterns.why: Option B does not publish bulk history; only _project/** messages matter (w5).

anti_patterns.dont: proceed to Phase 1 until w8 is complete
anti_patterns.why: the remediation strategy may require additional preparation that is cheaper to do before further changes layer on.

anti_patterns.dont: run git filter-repo during this audit
anti_patterns.why: filter-repo rewrites history; that should be a deliberate, separately-scheduled step in Phase 4 (or skipped entirely if D2a flips to working-tree-only).

preserves.behavior: Bulk private history is being left behind anyway, so commit-message audits on non-_project/** paths are NOT needed (a meaningful narrowing vs Option A).
The decisions doc from the gate item is the canonical record - this audit updates it with findings, not a new doc.
The private repo is unchanged by this audit. Audit is read-only; remediation (if any) is staged for a later step.

verifications.expected: 0 (or each line accounted for in decisions doc)

verifications.description: Decision doc updated with D2a final choice and audit summary

work_units.notes:
brew install gitleaks
cd /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox
gitleaks detect --no-git --source . \
  --report-path=/tmp/gitleaks-worktree.json
Review report. Triage each finding as: real secret in a file (must
fix before final sync + rotate), false positive (add to
.gitleaksignore), or low-risk legacy test fixture.
work_units.summary: Install gitleaks and run working-tree scan

work_units.notes:
gitleaks detect --source . \
  --log-opts='--all -- _project/' \
  --report-path=/tmp/gitleaks-project-history.json
If clean: D2a (filter-merge) is safe.
If dirty with real secrets: choose between scrubbing via
git filter-repo --replace-text/--invert-paths, or downgrading
_project/** to working-tree-only (override D2a).
work_units.summary: Run gitleaks on _project/** history (the only history being published)

work_units.notes:
find _project -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.md' | xargs grep -l -i \
  'TODO\|FIXME\|HACK\|XXX'
Read what comes back. Look for stakeholder names, internal vendor
complaints, references to private business plans. Most TODO content
is fine to publish; the goal is to catch outliers.

Read every file under _blog/drafts/ and decide: ship as-is, edit
before final sync, or move to a wip/ branch that never merges (per D4).
Drafts are higher-risk than TODOs because they may contain unedited
opinions. Note: only the working-tree state of _blog/ is published;
history is not preserved (no filter-merge for _blog/).

Only _project/** history is being published, so only _project/**'s
commit messages need this audit:
  git log --all --format='%h %s' -- _project/ | grep -iE \
    'wip|hack|fix(?:me|up)|temp|stupid|broken|fuck|shit'
If hits exist: scrub via filter-repo --message-callback before the
Phase 4 filter-merge, or override D2a to working-tree-only.
work_units.summary: Scan _project/** commit messages for embarrassing language

work_units.notes:
cd /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox
git log --format='%s' public/main | sort -u > /tmp/public-msgs.txt
git log --format='%s' --all | sort -u > /tmp/private-msgs.txt
comm -23 /tmp/public-msgs.txt /tmp/private-msgs.txt
Output: commit subjects on public mirror absent from private.
Should be empty or trivially explainable. Investigate any leftovers —
they may represent fix-ups applied directly to the curated mirror
that should be replicated on private (or accepted as left-behind)
before the final sync. Verified prior: at least two such fix-ups
exist (landing badge fix, linkcheck fix); they ARE represented in
private but with different SHAs from prepare_release.py squashing,
so this comm check should still come back empty by message.
work_units.summary: Divergence check: anything on public mirror not represented in private

work_units.notes:
git rev-list --objects --all -- _project/ | \
  git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectname) %(objectsize) %(rest)' | \
  awk '$1=="blob" && $3 > 5000000' | sort -k3 -nr | head
Anything over 5 MB in _project/ history is suspicious. If found,
plan a filter-repo --strip-blobs-bigger-than run before the
Phase 4 filter-merge.
work_units.summary: Check for unintended large blobs in _project/** history

work_units.notes:
Update _project/decisions/single-repo-migration.md with the final
D2a choice based on findings. Three options:
- PROCEED: gitleaks clean, content acceptable, divergence empty
- SCRUB: use git filter-repo to remove specific paths/blobs/messages
  from _project/** history before the Phase 4 filter-merge
- WORKING-TREE-ONLY: drop _project/** to part of the final curated
  sync (no preserved history); loses TODO/DONE archaeology but
  eliminates content risk
Document the choice and reason.
